correctness.rationale: Direct signed-antichain convex-hull representation gives the orthogonal free sum of coordinate cubes. An exact Dirichlet radial integral yields both volume and all covariance eigenvalues. Determinant specialization follows algebraically. For integer m=k+2≥3 the second difference is 2 log(1+1/m)+m log(1−2/[m(m+1)]), positive at m=3 by 2000/1944>1 and for m≥4 by the stated two strict logarithm inequalities and an algebraic comparison equivalent to m≥4. Strictly increasing differences imply every anti-balancing transfer increases L, and finite transfers prove the two complete extremal equality classes for all N≥r≥2. Independently replayed verification code checks 798 integer second differences, 31,161 compositions, and 11 exact-rational convex-hull triangulations; checks are diagnostics only and not the all-dimensional proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement is strict fixed-dimension, fixed-rank majorization and the complete balanced-versus-star extremal/equality classification. The known general Hanner recursion covers the exact covariance formula, but the full prior RESULT.md states only global cross-polytope/cube extremal bounds; neither it nor the published enriched two-level covariance comparison gives the discrete balancing inequality or all-rank equality classes. The independently proved strict second-difference inequality supplies this missing structural step. Search failure is not novelty proof; unindexed rearrangement results remain a substantive residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The canonical enriched chain polytope is motivated by poset geometry, and its affine-invariant isotropic constant is a natural global measure of volume/covariance shape. The theorem solves the sharp fixed-total-size, fixed-layer-count shape optimization for every positive integer profile, characterizes equality, and yields strict comparisons between nonisomorphic rank arrangements. The discrete-convexity classification is not a routine numerical special case of the prior Hanner recursion or merely a restated global cube/cross-polytope bound. It provides a reusable majorization order for studying poset rank structure.
